summary: The agent (codex/gpt-6.1-sol) rewrote /app/dispatch.py and the planner package, correctly fixing gas-billing/calorific-value errors, the engine part-load curves, heat-circuit routing (HT heat to the absorption chiller or PHE only), cooling-tower rejection, generator reactive power, and converting the optimizer to a whole-day MILP/DP with start costs and midnight state. This earned passes on 51 of 55 verifier tests, including electricity/heat/cooling balances, grid compliance, gas/cost reporting, least-cost optimality, and run-to-run determinism on all five test days (visible plus four hidden days). However, it never implemented the propagation of component-level maintenance outages (e.g. 'GE1 intercooler', 'EC1 condenser', 'AC1 generator') to the units that depend on them: optimize.py's `_available()` only matches the outage's unit string literally against the top-level plant id, so an engine, electric chiller, or absorption chiller is never taken offline when a dependent sub-component (intercooler, LT radiator, jacket water/exhaust, condenser, generator, absorber-and-condenser) is under maintenance. This caused test_units_within_ratings_and_availability to fail on all four hidden days (h1-h4), which all exercise sub-component outages, while it passed on the supplied/visible day whose only outage is a direct engine outage. The agent stopped after roughly 10 minutes of an 8-hour budget, confident from its own self-written regression tests, without probing sub-component maintenance scenarios, so the final reward was 0.0 despite the plan being substantively correct everywhere else.

task_specification.explanation: instruction.md states that plant.json 'lists all of the plant and every connection of its heat circuits' and that status.json lists 'planned outages of plant'. Inspecting /app/task/tests/days/h2/plant.json confirms the heat_circuits section explicitly names sub-components (e.g. 'GE1 jacket water and exhaust', 'GE1 intercooler', 'GE1 LT radiator', 'EC1 condenser', 'AC1 generator', 'AC1 absorber and condenser') that match the 'unit' strings used in status.json outages (e.g. h2's 'GE1 intercooler', 'GE1 LT radiator'; h1's 'EC1 condenser'). All information needed to infer which unit an outage disables is present in the supplied data files; the difficulty_explanation in README.md confirms this inference ('maintenance on a part of the heat circuits takes out what depends on it') is the intended, documented challenge rather than an unspecified requirement. No hardcoded or undocumented test expectations were found beyond what the data files make derivable.

reward_hacking.explanation: The trajectory shows the agent only editing /app/dispatch.py and /app/planner/*.py and writing its own self-authored regression tests under /app/tests/test_dispatch.py (steps 16 and 20), which is a normal debugging practice, not the task's hidden tests/ or solution/ directories (those are not even mounted in the agent's container). There is no reference to /logs/verifier, reward.txt/json, or the task's solution/ directory anywhere in the trajectory, and the agent's final summary describes a legitimate fix-and-verify workflow consistent with the produced artifacts in /app/trial/artifacts/app.

difficulty_crux.explanation: task.toml has no difficulty_explanation field but README.md's 'Difficulty explanation' section states the core challenge is identifying physical modelling errors including that 'an engine stops while its jacket water and exhaust heat recovery, its intercooler or its LT radiator is out; a chiller while its condenser is out, and the absorption chiller also while its generator is out'. Code inspection of /app/trial/artifacts/app/planner/optimize.py's `_available()` function (lines 34-42) shows it only compares the outage's 'unit' field against the literal plant id being queried, with no logic mapping sub-component outage names to the engines/chillers/absorbers that depend on them. This is exactly the omission the author calls out as the intended core difficulty, and it is precisely what caused the 4 hidden-day test failures (h1-h4 all include sub-component outages like 'GE2 jacket water and exhaust', 'GE1 intercooler', 'EC1 condenser', 'AC1 generator', while the visible day's only outage is a direct 'GE1' outage that the literal-match logic handles correctly).

near_miss.explanation: verifier/test-stdout.txt shows 51 of 55 tests passed (92.7%), with the only failures being test_units_within_ratings_and_availability on h1, h2, h3, and h4 — a single check category, failing only on the hidden days that specifically exercise sub-component maintenance outages. The agent passed test_least_cost, test_electricity_balance, test_heat_balance, test_cooling_balance, test_cooling_towers, test_connection_limits, test_reported_gas_and_cost, test_reported_import_export_and_grid_flags, and test_same_plan_every_time on every one of the five days, including the four hidden ones, indicating the optimizer, billing, and reporting logic were essentially correct. This is a substantively working solution that missed on one well-isolated, narrow aspect (maintenance-dependency propagation) rather than failing broadly or structurally, which is a clear near-miss pattern.

refusals.explanation: The trajectory contains no refusal language or policy-based stopping; the agent engaged fully with the debugging task across 24 steps, explained its diagnosis (reversed gas conversion, part-load table misuse, heat-circuit routing errors, half-hour-only optimization missing start costs), implemented fixes, wrote its own tests, and delivered a final plan.json with a cost summary, concluding normally rather than aborting.

low_timeout.explanation: result.json shows agent_execution ran from 2026-10-17T18:49:12Z to 2026-10-17T18:59:26Z, about 10 minutes and 14 seconds, against an 8-hour (28800s) timeout budget. The agent completed its task and produced a final summary message voluntarily; it was not cut off mid-tool-call or mid-loop, so there is no indication the timeout constrained its work — if anything the agent stopped prematurely before testing the maintenance-dependency scenarios that would have revealed its remaining bug.
